title: Servepath percentile heat-strip: per-model & endpoint p50/p95/p99 with IO-mode split and anomaly flags
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context:
We need a new operational dashboard that surfaces percentile latency (p50/p95/p99) for every served model and public route (endpoint) with a clear split between streaming and non-streaming IO modes. Existing boards are useful but scatter multiple visualizations across different views. This ticket builds a single 'heat-strip' view that makes regressions and cross-route anomalies obvious and provides links into traces and the trace hooks introduced in the tracing infra work.

Goals:
1) Produce a per-model x per-route matrix displaying p50/p95/p99 as a compact heat-strip, with color intensity representing relative degradation vs baseline.
2) Provide an IO-mode toggle to break each cell into streaming vs non-streaming bars and show the delta.
3) Surface an automatically computed waterfall decomposition per cell (ingress, runtime, kv-cache, egress) and link to a sample trace in Tempo/Jaeger.
4) Add anomaly flags where percentile deviates > 2x baseline or crosses SLO targets; anomalies should drive alerting rules and a curated incident runbook link.

Instrumentation changes required:
- Tracing: add attributes to the top-level request span: serve.route (string), model.id (string), io.mode (enum: streaming|sync), kv_cache_hit (bool). Ensure these attributes are set at the ingress hook and preserved on span propagation. Update runtime trace hooks to emit sub-span timings for 'ingress', 'compile/kernel', 'runtime-token-loop', 'kv-cache-lookup', 'egress'.
- Metrics: emit low-cardinality metrics used for aggregation: serve_latency_ms (histogram buckets & raw ms), serve_span_count, serve_io_mode (label), serve_model (label), serve_route (label), kv_cache_hit_ratio. Update Prometheus exporter's relabeling to keep model and route cardinality bounded (top N with fallback: _other).
- Logs: add structured log fields route/model/io_mode to correlate traces with errors and sample payloads. Ensure sample IDs surface in dashboard links.

Aggregation & example queries (ClickHouse / PromQL style):
- ClickHouse percentile rollup (example):
  SELECT
    model_id,
    route,
    io_mode,
    quantileExact(0.5)(lat_ms) AS p50,
    quantileExact(0.95)(lat_ms) AS p95,
    quantileExact(0.99)(lat_ms) AS p99
  FROM serve_latency_raw
  WHERE ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  GROUP BY model_id, route, io_mode
  ORDER BY sum(count) DESC

- Waterfall decomposition (one-pass aggregation):
  SELECT
    model_id, route, io_mode,
    quantileExact(0.95)(ingress_ms) AS ingress_p95,
    quantileExact(0.95)(runtime_ms) AS runtime_p95,
    quantileExact(0.95)(kv_ms) AS kv_p95,
    quantileExact(0.95)(egress_ms) AS egress_p95
  FROM span_timings
  WHERE ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  GROUP BY model_id, route, io_mode

Design notes / UI behavior:
- Main view: rows = top 100 models (by QPS), columns = routes for the selected model or global top 200 routes. Each cell is a compact vertical strip showing p50/p95/p99 as stacked bars colored by severity. Hover reveals absolute ms, delta vs baseline, and link to sample traces.
- IO-mode toggle: hover opens split view showing two mini-strips (streaming on left, sync on right) and a small percent change metric.
- Drilldown: clicking a cell opens the waterfall panel and the top 3 sample traces (Tempo) with span annotations.
- Anomaly striping: if any percentile crosses thresholds, the cell gets a red top border and an automated 'investigate' link that opens the suggested runbook and creates a pre-filled incident ticket.

Alerting & SLOs:
- SLOs per route+model: e.g., p95 < 1.5s for low-cost models, p95 < 800ms for premium routes. On breach, generate a Jira/Linear alert to oncall and annotate dashboard.
- Anomaly detection: time series baseline computed with median absolute deviation over the last 14 days; flag if current p95 > 2 * baseline or absolute increase > 200ms for 30m window.

Rollout plan:
1) Instrumentation merge -> deploy to canary region (eu-west-1) with sampling enabled (10%).
2) Backfill last 7 days of metrics into ClickHouse to build baseline.
3) Launch dashboard as read-only to SRE and runtime teams.
4) After 3 days of verification, flip sampling to 100% for top 50 routes.
5) Full launch in console-2026.03 release.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard renders p50/p95/p99 for top 100 model-route combinations within 15s.
- IO-mode split is accurate and matches trace-derived counts within 3% for sampled traffic.
- Waterfall decomposition links to at least one sampled trace for every flagged cell.
- Alerts fire for synthetic regressions injected in staging with expected threshold behavior.

Risks & mitigations:
- Cardinality explosion: mitigate with top-N relabeling and _other buckets; roll up rare models into 'legacy-other'.
- Metric ingestion costs: use coarse histogram buckets for low-volume routes and sample traces for deep decomposition.
- Query latency: precompute hourly aggregates for dashboard fast-path and provide 'refresh' for raw queries.

Artifacts & links:
- Wireframe (Figma): https://redwood.app.link/figma/servepath-heatstrip (private)
- Example ClickHouse queries and profiler: https://drive.redwood/observability/servepath-queries.md
- Tracing hook PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824
- Runbook (investigate-latency): https://docs.redwood/runbooks/investigate-latency

Next steps:
- (A) Work with runtime to land trace attributes and span breakouts.
- (B) Finalize ClickHouse rollup schema with infra.
- (C) Build dashboard panels in Console and iterate with SRE.
